facts.statement: The only known species is Dongyangosaurus sinensis, represented by a single fragmentary skeleton found in Zhejiang province, eastern China.
facts.quote: The only species is Dongyangosaurus sinensis, from which only a single fragmentary skeleton is known, coming from the Zhejiang province of eastern China.

facts.statement: Dongyangosaurus was a medium-sized sauropod measuring approximately 50 feet (15 meters) in length and 15 feet (5 meters) in height.
facts.quote: Dongyangosaurus was a midsized sauropod, measuring approximately 50 ft (15 m) in length and 15 ft (5 m) in height.

facts.statement: Its dorsal vertebrae featured eye-shaped pleurocoels and low, bifurcated neural spines.
facts.quote: The dorsal vertebrae were characterized by eye shaped pleurocoels and low bifurcated neural spines.

facts.statement: The sacrum consisted of six fused vertebrae, a trait unique to somphospondylan sauropods.
facts.quote: The sacrum consisted of six fused sacral vertebrae, a feature unique to somphospondylans.

facts.statement: In Dongyangosaurus, the pubis bone was shorter than the ischium.
facts.quote: The pubis was shorter than the ischium.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 2007 in the village of Baidian, Dongyang city, giving the genus its name.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in 2007 in the village of Baidian within the city of Dongyang, from which the generic name is derived.

facts.statement: The specific name 'sinensis' means 'from China' in Greek.
facts.quote: The specific name, sinensis, is Greek for "from China".

facts.statement: The species was formally described by Lu et al. in 2008 as Dongyangosaurus sinensis.
facts.quote: La especie tipo fue descrita por Lu et al. en 2008, como D. sinensis.

facts.statement: Dongyangosaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago in the Cenomanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente entre 100,5 a 93,9 millones de años durante el Cenomaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dongyangosaurus come from the Fangyan Formation.
facts.quote: Dongyangosaurus proviene de la Formación Fangyan.

facts.statement: More recent studies discovered that it was a Saltasauridae closely related to the Mongolian sauropod Opisthocoelicaudia.
facts.quote: Más recientemente, sin embargo, se descubrió que era un Saltasauridae estrechamente relacionado con el saurópodo mongol Opisthocoelicaudia.

facts.statement: The exact family relationships of this genus remain unclear.
facts.quote: Las relaciones de parentesco de este género no están claras.

facts.statement: Like other sauropods, Dongyangosaurus was a large, four-legged herbivore.
facts.quote: Like other sauropods, Dongyangosaurus would have been a large quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: The single known skeleton was found in an articulated state.

rejected.statement: In 2013, researchers reclassified Dongyangosaurus as a saltasaurid closely related to the Mongolian sauropod Opisthocoelicaudia.
rejected.quote: In 2013, however, it was found to be a saltasaurid closely related to the Mongolian sauropod Opisthocoelicaudia.
